title: Bagging a purchase without losing track of it
target: How paper bags and the packing step work in Supermarket Simulator, including the part the counter plays in it.
version: 1.6.0 (223), read from the copy of the game this site was built from (see the sources page)

steps.do: Expect a bag to be made by the game rather than a prop you place.
steps.because: a paper bag is built by the game rather than placed in the shop as decoration (PaperBagFactory)

steps.do: Use the bag-placing mode instead of dropping things into a pile.
steps.because: there is a mode of its own for placing a bag (PaperBagPlacingMode)

steps.do: Know that once something is bagged it is a different object.
steps.because: a product that is in a bag is its own object and there is a bag form of a product (PaperBagProductInstance, ProductPaperBag)

steps.do: Treat a bag as part of an order rather than as loose packaging.
steps.because: a bag belongs to an order, with its own data and a container of them (OrderPaperBag, OrderPaperBagData, OrderPaperBagContainer)

steps.do: Expect a packed bag to have a shared form and an online form.
steps.because: the packed order bag has a shared form and one for online orders (NetworkOrderPaperBag, OnlineOrderPaperBagContainer)

steps.do: Leave the packing to play out rather than interrupting it.
steps.because: packing a bag has an animation of its own (OrderPaperBagAnimation)

steps.do: Plan the packing around the counter you actually have.
steps.because: the counter is modelled as a belt with a grid, a drawer and a manager for change (CheckoutBelt, CheckoutBeltGrid, CheckoutDrawer, CheckoutChangeManager)

commonMistakes: Stacking purchases beside a bag instead of bagging them.
Treating a bagged product as the same object as the one on the shelf.
Forgetting that an online order is packed into a bag form of its own.
Packing on a counter that has no room left on its belt.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Grounding for each step is on the technical reference pages; no number is estimated.
